paragraphs: Unless otherwise required by the context, the terms "we," "us," "our" and "the company" as used herein refer to Tidewater Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries and predecessors.

We have provided marine and transportation services to the global offshore energy industry since our incorporation in 1956. Our mission includes providing services to our customers with the highest level of operational performance, while complying with laws and regulations, respecting the environment and local communities in which we work and supporting the safety of our people.

We offer a large, diversified fleet of offshore service vessels (OSV) and related support vessels (collectively, vessels), with 208 vessels serving customers in over 30 countries as of December 31, 2025. We believe our global operating footprint allows us to react quickly to changing local market conditions and to be responsive to the changing requirements of our customers. We manage our operations through five geographically aligned reporting segments:
Americas Asia Pacific Middle East Europe/Mediterranean West Africa
Each reporting segment is overseen by a managing director, who is a senior company executive ultimately reporting to our Chief Executive Officer, the chief operating decision maker.

Our vessels routinely move between geographic regions as our customers complete projects and new projects arise. We conduct our business through domestic and international subsidiaries, as well as through joint ventures that we may or may not control (generally where required to satisfy local ownership or local content requirements).

Our vessels and associated services support all phases of offshore crude oil and natural gas (also referred to as oil and gas) exploration, field development, production and maintenance, as well as windfarm development and maintenance activities. Our service offerings include towing and anchor handling for mobile offshore drilling units; the transportation of supplies and personnel necessary to sustain drilling, workover and production operations, as well as field abandonment, dismantlement and restoration activities; offshore construction, seismic and subsea support; and a variety of other specialized services such as pipe laying, cable laying and geotechnical survey support for windfarm construction.

Our principal customers include large, international, integrated and independent oil and gas exploration, development and production companies (IOCs); mid-sized and smaller independent exploration and production (E&P) companies; foreign government-owned or government-controlled organizations (NOCs) engaged in the exploration, development and production of oil and gas; offshore drilling contractors; and other companies that provide various services to the offshore energy industry, including offshore construction companies, windfarm development companies, diving companies and well stimulation companies.

Our revenues, earnings and cash flows are dependent upon the activity level of our vessel fleet. Consistent with other vessel operators in our industry, our business activity is largely dependent on offshore exploration, development, production and abandonment activity, and the overall capital budgets of our customers. Our customers' offshore business activity, in turn, is dependent on current and expected oil and gas prices, which fluctuate depending on expected future levels of supply and demand for oil and gas, and on estimates of the cost to find, develop and produce oil and gas reserves both onshore and offshore.

Depending on vessel capabilities and availability, our vessels operate in the shallow, intermediate and deepwater offshore markets, with the majority of our current fleet serving deepwater operations. Deepwater oil and gas development typically involves significant capital investment and multi-year development plans and therefore less susceptible to short-term fluctuations in commodity prices, although generally more costly than onshore and other offshore exploration and development.

Our revenues are derived primarily from vessel time charter or similar contracts ranging in duration from a few months to several years. To a lesser extent, we derive revenue from vessel time charter contracts on a "spot" basis, which are short-term agreements ranging from one day to several months. The base rate of hire for a term contract is generally a fixed day rate, though some longer-term contracts have rate escalation clauses. In addition, many charter arrangements allow us to recover specific limited additional costs, such as fuel expenses, while on hire.

Our primary vessel classifications include Anchor Handling Towing Supply Vessels (AHTS) and Platform Supply Vessels (PSVs). We also operate a small number of other specialty vessels. A description of the type of vessels categorized in each vessel class and the services typically performed follows.

The most versatile vessels in the Tidewater fleet are large, powerful AHTS vessels, capable of all types of towing, anchor handling activities, and varied subsea operations. Fitted with experienced crews and state of the art technology, AHTS vessels of various classes are capable of positioning and mooring drilling rigs in virtually any location, depth or sea condition and under a wide range of conditions. With a wide range of power, sizes and capacities, these vessels are also well-suited for general offshore support services, drilling rig support functions and cargo transport assignments.

AHTS vessel capabilities are typically distinguished by the vessel's engine power output in terms of brake horsepower (BHP), which generally correlates with its towing capacity. As of December 31, 2025, we operated 52 AHTS vessels throughout our service regions. During the year ended December 31, 2025, our AHTS vessels contributed approximately 24.2% of our vessel revenue.

Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
A rise in production of oil and gas resources could increase supply without a commensurate growth in demand which could negatively impact oil and gas prices.
Failure to effectively and timely address the energy transition could adversely affect our business, results of operations and cash flows.
We derive a significant amount of revenue from a relatively small number of customers.
We may not be able to collect amounts owed to us by our customers.
Our customer base has undergone consolidation and additional consolidation is possible.
The high level of competition in the offshore marine service industry could negatively impact pricing for our services.
Maintaining our current fleet size and configuration and acquiring vessels required for additional future growth requires significant capital.
We may not be able to renew or replace expiring contracts for our vessels.

Our ability to raise capital in the future through debt or equity financing may be limited, which could make us unable to fund our capital requirements or business operations or potentially dilute existing stockholders.
Early termination of contracts on our vessels could have an adverse effect on our operations and our backlog may not be converted to actual operating results for any future period.
We may record impairment charges or other losses related to our vessels.
We may not be able to sell vessels because we may be unable to locate buyers with access to financing or to complete any sales on acceptable terms or within a reasonable timeframe.
An increase in vessel supply without a corresponding increase in the working offshore rig count could lead to a decline in the charter day rates we can charge and negatively impact our revenue.
Our insurance coverage and contractual indemnity protections may not be sufficient to protect us under all circumstances or against all risks.
Risks Relating to Our International and Foreign Operations
Disruptions or disagreements with our foreign joint venture partners, could lead to an unwinding of the joint venture.
Our international operations expose us to currency devaluation, exchange and conversion risk.
Failure to attract and retain qualified personnel could impede our operations.
We may be subject to additional unionization efforts, new collective bargaining agreements or work stoppages.
Our participation in industry-wide, multi-employer, defined benefit pension plans expose us to potential future losses.
Certain of our employees are covered by federal laws that may subject us to job-related claims in addition to those provided by state laws.
We may not be able to generate sufficient cash flow to meet our debt service and other obligations.

Below is a summary of some of the principal risks and uncertainties that could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects. You should read this summary together with the more detailed description of each risk factor contained below.
Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry

Demand for our services is substantially dependent on the level of capital spending by our customers. Downturns in the oil and gas industry have often resulted in lower expenditures by our customers and reduced demand for our services, which in the past has, and in the future may have, material adverse effects on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
A rise in production of oil and gas resources could increase supply without a commensurate growth in demand which could negatively impact oil and gas prices.

paragraphs: The following Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) should be read in conjunction with the accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements included in Item 8 of this Form 10-K. The following discussion and analysis contain forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our future results of operations could differ materially from our historical results or those anticipated in our forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those set forth under "Risk Factors" in Item 1A and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. With respect to this section, the cautionary language applicable to such forward-looking statements described under "Forward-Looking Statements" found before Item 1 of this Form 10-K is incorporated by reference into this Item 7.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY AND CURRENT BUSINESS OUTLOOK Tidewater

We are one of the most experienced international operators in the offshore energy industry with a history spanning over 65 years. Our vessels and associated vessel services provide support for all phases of offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production as well as windfarm development and maintenance. These services include towing and anchor handling for mobile offshore drilling units; transporting supplies and personnel necessary to sustain drilling, workover and production activities; providing offshore construction and seismic and subsea support; delivering geotechnical survey support for windfarm construction, and offering a variety of other specialized services such as pipe laying and cable laying. In addition, we believe we have the broadest geographic operating footprint in the offshore vessel industry. Our global operating footprint allows us to react quickly to changing local market conditions and to be responsive to the changing requirements of the many customers with which we believe we have strong relationships.

On February 22, 2026, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all outstanding shares of Wilson Sons Ultratug Participações S.A and its affiliate Atlantic Offshore Services S.A. (collectively, the Wilson Companies) from Wilson Sons S.A., Ultranav International II, S.A. and Remolcadores Ultratug Limitada (collectively, the Wilson Sellers). The Wilson Companies own 22 platform supply vessels operating in Brazil. We will pay the Wilson Sellers an aggregate cash purchase price of $500.0 million on a debt free, cash free basis, subject to adjustments, including a reduction for the assumption of the Wilson Companies' debt which was approximately $261.0 million as of September 30, 2025. The final debt amount will be determined upon completion of this transaction. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including approval from the Brazilian Antitrust Authority and the consent of the lenders to the Wilson Companies, and is expected to close late in the second quarter of 2026.

In the fourth quarter of 2025, we completed a strategic internal restructuring of our vessel ownership (Vessel Realignment) to consolidate a significant portion of the fleet into a single, wholly owned U.S. entity. As a result, we recognized a one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit in the Consolidated Income Statement for the year ended December 31, 2025.

On July 7, 2025, we issued $650.0 million in 9.125% Senior Notes that mature in July 2030 (2030 Notes). With the proceeds of the offering, we redeemed most of our outstanding debt as of June 30, 2025, including accrued interest and early redemption premiums. Also on July 7, 2025, we executed the $250.0 million Revolving Credit Facility that replaced our previous $25.0 million credit facility. As of the date of this filing, no amounts have been drawn under the Revolving Credit Facility.

On March 7, 2023, we entered into an Agreement for the Sale and Purchase of Vessels, Charter Parties and Other Assets, which was amended on June 30, 2023 (the Acquisition Agreement), with certain subsidiaries of Solstad Offshore ASA, a Norwegian public limited company (collectively, the Sellers), pursuant to which we agreed to acquire from the Sellers (the Solstad Acquisition): (i) 37 platform supply vessels owned by the Sellers (the Solstad Vessels); and (ii) the charter parties governing certain of the Solstad Vessels. At closing, these vessels operated primarily in the North Sea, Australia and Brazil. On July 5, 2023, we completed the Solstad Acquisition for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $594.2 million, consisting of the $577.0 million base purchase price plus an initial $3.0 million purchase price adjustment; $3.2 million for working capital items comprised of fuel and lubricants; and $11.0 million in estimated transaction costs, consisting primarily of advisory and legal fees. The purchase price was funded through a combination of cash on hand and net proceeds from both the Senior Secured Term Loan and the 10.375% Senior Unsecured Notes due July 2028.

Prior to August 1, 2023, we had outstanding Series A Warrants, with an exercise price of $57.06 and Series B Warrants, with an exercise price of $62.28, both with an expiration date of July 31, 2023. During July 2023, an aggregate of approximately 2.0 million Series A Warrants and Series B Warrants were exercised, and we issued 1.9 million shares of common stock in exchange for $111.5 million in cash proceeds. All remaining unexercised Series A Warrants and Series B Warrants, approximately 3.1 million in the aggregate, expired according to their terms on July 31, 2023.
At December 31, 2025, we owned 208 vessels with an average age of 13.1 years available to serve the global offshore energy industry.
Our MD&A is designed to provide information about our financial condition and results of operations from management's perspective.

Our revenues, net earnings and cash flows from operations are largely dependent upon the activity level of our offshore marine vessel fleet. Our business activity is largely dependent on the level of oil and gas exploration, development and production activity of our customers. Our customers' business activity, in turn, is dependent on current and expected oil and gas prices, which fluctuate depending on expected future levels of supply and demand for oil and gas, and on estimates of the cost to find, develop and produce oil and gas reserves. Our objective throughout MD&A is to discuss how these factors affected our historical results and, where applicable, how we expect these factors to impact our future results and future liquidity.

Our revenues are driven primarily by our active fleet size, active vessel utilization and day rates. Because a sizeable portion of our operating and depreciation costs do not change proportionally with changes in revenue, our operating profit is largely dependent on revenue levels.

Operating costs consist primarily of crew costs, repair and maintenance costs, insurance costs, fuel, lube oil and supplies costs and other vessel operating costs. Fleet size, fleet composition, geographic areas of operation, supply and demand for marine personnel, and local labor requirements are the major factors impacting overall crew costs in all segments. In addition, our newer, more technologically sophisticated vessels generally require a greater number of specially trained, more highly compensated fleet personnel than our older, smaller and less sophisticated vessels. Crew costs may increase if competition for skilled personnel intensifies.

Costs related to the recertification of vessels are deferred and amortized over a 30-month period on a straight-line basis. Maintenance costs incurred at the time of the recertification drydocking not related to the recertification of the vessel are expensed as incurred. Costs related to vessel improvements that either extend the vessel's useful life or increase the vessel's functionality are capitalized and depreciated.

paragraphs: 除非上下文另有要求， herein 所使用的 "we," "us," "our" 和 "the company" 係指 Tidewater Inc. 及其合併子公司與前身。
自我們於 1956 年設立以來，我們已為全球離岸能源產業提供海洋與運輸服務。我們的使命包括為客戶提供最高水準的運營表現，同時遵守法律與法規，尊重我們所從事地區的環境與當地社區，並支持我們員工的安全。
我們提供一支規模龐大的多元化離岸服務船隻（OSV）與相關支援船隻（合稱為船隻），截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們共有 208 艘船隻服務於超過 30 個國家。我們相信我們的全球運營據點使我們能迅速應對當地市場條件的變化，並對客戶的變更需求做出反應。我們透過五個地理對應的應報告分部來管理運營：
美洲 亞太 中東 歐洲/地中海 西非
每個應報告分部由一位 managing director 管理，該 managing director 是公司高階主管，最終向我們的首席執行長報告，首席執行長為主要運營決策者。
我們的船隻經常在不同地理區域間移動，因為客戶完成專案或新專案出現。我們透過國內與國際子公司，以及我們可能控制或不控制的合資企業（通常因需符合當地股權或當地內容要求）進行業務。
我們的船隻與相關服務支援離岸原油與天然氣（亦稱為油氣）的各個階段，包括探勘、油田開發、生產與維護，以及風電場的開發與維護活動。我們的服務項目包括為移動式離岸鑽井單位提供拖船與錨機服務；運輸維持鑽井、作業與生產作業所需的物資與人員，以及油田棄置、拆卸與復原活動；離岸建設、地震與水下支援；以及多種其他專業服務，例如管線鋪設、電纜鋪設與風電場建設的地質調查支援。
我們的主要客戶包括大型國際整合型與獨立油氣探勘、開發與生產公司（IOCs）；中型與小型獨立探勘與生產公司（E&P）；從事油氣探勘、開發與生產的外國政府擁有或控制的組織（NOCs）；離岸鑽井承包商；以及為離岸能源產業提供各類服務的其他公司，包括離岸建設公司、風電場開發公司、潛水公司與井壓裂公司。
本公司之營業收入、獲利及現金流取決於船舶艦隊之運作程度。與本行業其他船舶運營商一致，本公司之業務活動主要取決於海上探勘、開發、生產及棄置活動，以及客戶之總體資本預算。客戶之海上業務活動，進而取決於目前及預期之油氣價格，該價格會根據未來油氣供應與需求之預期水平而波動，並根據尋找、開發及生產油氣儲備之預估成本（包括陸上及海上）而變動。
根據船舶之能力及可得性，本公司之船舶運作於淺水、中水及深水海上市場，目前本公司之艦隊主要用於深水作業。深水油氣開發通常涉及大量資本投資及多年度開發計畫，因此較不受短期商品價格波動影響，雖然通常比陸上及其他海上探勘與開發活動成本更高。
本公司之收入主要來自船舶時間租賃或類似合約，合約期間從數個月到數年不等。較少部分之收入來自於船舶時間租賃合約之「現貨」方式，為短期協議，期間從一天到數個月不等。長期合約之基本租賃率通常為固定日租金，雖然部分長期合約包含租金上漲條款。此外，許多租賃安排允許本公司回收特定有限額之額外成本，例如燃油費用，於租賃期間。
本公司主要之船舶分類包括錨機拖船與供應船（AHTS）及平台供應船（PSVs）。本公司亦運營少量其他專業船舶。以下為各船舶分類之船舶類型及通常執行之服務之說明。
Tidewater艦隊中最靈活之船舶為大型、強大之AHTS船舶，可執行所有類型之拖曳、錨機作業及多樣化海底作業。配備經驗豐富之船員及最先進之科技，不同類別之AHTS船舶可於幾乎任何地點、深度或海況及廣泛條件下進行定位及錨定鑽井平台。這些船舶亦因具備廣泛之動力、尺寸及載重能力，而非常適合一般海上支援服務、鑽井平台支援功能及貨物運輸任務。
AHTS船舶之能力通常以船舶之引擎動力輸出（以馬力為單位，即BHP）為準，通常與其拖曳能力相關。截至2025年12月31日，本公司於服務區域內運營52艘AHTS船舶。在截至2025年12月31日之會計年度內，本公司之AHTS船舶貢獻約24.2%之船舶收入。

paragraphs: 下列管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析（MD&A）應與本表單10-K第8項所附之合併財務報表一併閱讀。下列討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。我們未來之營運結果可能與歷史結果或前瞻性陳述中預期之結果有重大差異，原因包括某些因素，包括於第1A項「風險因素」及本表單10-K其他地方所列述之因素。關於本節，本表單10-K第1項前之「前瞻性陳述」所描述之警示語句，已納入本項目7中。
執行摘要與目前營運展望 Tidewater

我們是離岸能源產業中經驗最豐富的國際營運商之一，擁有超過65年的歷史。我們之船舶及相關船舶服務可支援離岸石油與天然氣探勘、開發與生產，以及風電場開發與維護之各階段。這些服務包括移動式離岸鑽井單位之拖船與錨機操作；運輸維持鑽井、壓井與生產活動所需之物資與人員；提供離岸建設與地震與水下支援；為風電場建設提供地質調查支援，並提供多種其他專門服務，例如管線鋪設與電纜鋪設。此外，我們相信我們在離岸船舶產業中擁有最廣泛的地理營運範圍。我們之全球營運範圍使我們能迅速反應當地市場變動，並對我們認為擁有強大關係之許多客戶之變更需求作出回應。

2026年2月22日，我們與Wilson Sons S.A.、Ultranav International II, S.A.及Remolcadores Ultratug Limitada（合稱為Wilson Sellers）簽訂最終協議，以取得Wilson Sons Ultratug Participações S.A.及其附屬公司Atlantic Offshore Services S.A.（合稱為Wilson Companies）所有發行在外之股權。Wilson Companies擁有22艘平台供應船舶，於巴西運作。我們將以無負債、無現金基礎支付Wilson Sellers總計5億美元現金購股價，扣除調整項目，包括對Wilson Companies負債之減額，該負債截至2025年9月30日約為2.61億美元。最終負債金額將於本交易完成後確定。本交易需符合慣常關閉條件，包括巴西公平交易機構之批准及Wilson Companies貸款人之同意，預計於2026年第二季末關閉。
2025年第四季，我們完成一項戰略內部重組，將船舶擁有權（船舶重整）進行整併，將大量船隊集中於單一、完全擁有之美國實體。因此，我們於2025年12月31日財年合併損益表中確認一項一次性、非現金之遞延稅益。

於 2025 年 7 月 7 日，本公司發行 650.0 百萬美元之 9.125% 長期公司債，該債券於 2030 年 7 月到期（2030 年債券）。透過本次發行所得資金，本公司贖回截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日為止大部分未償還債務，包括應計利息及提前贖回 premium。同時於 2025 年 7 月 7 日，本公司執行 250.0 百萬美元之循環信貸融資，取代先前 25.0 百萬美元之信貸融資。截至本申報文件之申報日，尚未自循環信貸融資提領任何金額。

2023年3月7日，我們與Solstad Offshore ASA之某些子公司簽訂船舶買賣協議、租賃契約及其他資產之買賣協議（買賣協議），該協議於2023年6月30日進行修正（買賣協議），根據該協議，我們同意從賣方（賣方）取得（Solstad買賣）：(i) 37艘由賣方擁有之平台供應船舶（Solstad船舶）；以及(ii) 某些Solstad船舶之租賃契約。於交易完成時，這些船舶主要於北海、澳洲及巴西運作。2023年7月5日，我們完成Solstad買賣，總計現金購股價約為5.942億美元，包含5.77億美元之基本購股價及初始300萬美元購股調整；320萬美元用於營運資金項目，包含燃料及潤滑油；以及1100萬美元之交易成本預估，主要為顧問及法律費用。購股價透過現金及來自優先無擔保貸款及10.375%優先無擔保債券（於2028年7月到期）之淨資金進行資金籌措。

2023年8月1日之前，我們有Series A選擇權，行權價格為57.06美元，以及Series B選擇權，行權價格為62.28美元，兩者均於2023年7月31日到期。2023年7月，約200萬份Series A及Series B選擇權被行權，我們發行190萬股普通股以換取1.115億美元現金。所有未行權之Series A及Series B選擇權，約計310萬份，根據其條款於2023年7月31日到期。
於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有 208 艘船舶，平均年齡為 13.1 年，可用於服務全球離岸能源產業。
本公司之管理討論與分析（MD&A）係設計用以提供有關本公司財務狀況及營運成果之資訊，從管理階層之觀點出發。

本公司之營業收入、淨利及營運現金流 largely 依賴本公司離岸海運船舶艦隊之活動程度。本公司之業務活動 largely 依賴客戶之油氣探勘、開發及生產活動程度。客戶之業務活動，進而依賴目前及預期之油氣價格，該價格會根據未來油氣供應與需求預期水平以及尋找、開發及生產油氣儲備之成本估計而波動。本公司於 MD&A 中之目標係討論這些因素如何影響本公司歷史結果，並在適用時說明這些因素如何影響本公司未來結果及未來流動性。
本公司之營業收入主要由本公司活躍艦隊規模、活躍船舶使用率及每日租金所驅動。由於本公司營運及折舊成本中相當大一部分不會隨收入變化而成比例變動，因此本公司之營運獲利 largely 依賴收入水平。
營運成本主要由船員成本、維修與保養成本、保險成本、燃料、潤滑油及補給品成本及其他船舶營運成本組成。艦隊規模、艦隊組成、營運地理區域、海運人力之供需情況以及當地勞動需求是影響各個分部總體船員成本的主要因素。此外，本公司較新、技術更為先進之船舶通常需要較多具特別訓練、薪資較高的船員，與本公司較舊、較小且技術較不先進之船舶相比。若對專業人力之競爭加劇，船員成本可能增加。
與船舶重新認證相關之成本會延後並在 30 個月內以直線法攤銷。於重新認證乾船修理期間所產生與重新認證無關之維護成本會於產生時立即費用化。與船舶改進相關之成本，若能延長船舶之使用年限或提高船舶之功能，則會資本化並 depreciated。

headings: 活躍股東可能分散我們管理團隊的注意力，並/或對我們的業務產生負面影響。
與我們業務及產業相關的風險
石油與天然氣資源生產量增加，可能導致供應增加而需求成長不足，進而對石油與天然氣價格產生負面影響。
若未能有效且及時應對能源轉型，可能對我們的業務、營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。
我們來自相對少量客戶的收入佔比相當高。
我們可能無法收回客戶所欠的金額。
本公司客戶羣已歷經整併，未來仍有可能進行更多整併。
離岸海洋服務產業高度競爭的環境，可能對本公司服務的價格造成負面影響。
維持現有船隊規模與配置，並取得未來成長所需船舶，需要大量資金。
本公司可能無法續約或取代即將到期的船舶合約。
本公司未來透過債務或權益融資籌措資金的能力可能受到限制，這可能使本公司無法負擔資金需求或營運開支，或導致現有股東權益稀釋。
船舶合約提前終止，可能對本公司營運產生負面影響，且本公司積累的訂單可能無法在未來期間轉化為實際營運成果。
本公司可能因船舶而記錄減損費用或其他損失。
本公司可能無法出售船舶，因可能無法找到有資金來源的買方，或無法在合理時間內以可接受的條件完成銷售。
船舶供應量增加而 offshore 嚴重 rigs 數量未相對增加，可能導致我們可收取的租賃日費率下降，並對我們的營業收入造成負面影響。
我們的保險覆蓋範圍及契約賠償保護措施，可能在某些情況下或對所有風險而言並不足以保護我們。
與國際及外國業務相關的風險
與我們的外國合資夥伴發生中斷或意見分歧，可能導致合資企業的解散。
我們的國際業務使我們面臨貨幣貶值、匯率及兌換風險。
與人力資本相關的風險
未能吸引並留住合格人員，可能影響我們的業務運作。
我們可能面臨額外的工會化努力、新的集體談判協議或罷工行動。
本公司參與產業範圍內、多僱主參與之確定給付退休金計畫，可能面臨未來潛在損失。
部分本公司員工受美國聯邦法規保障，可能使本公司除州法規所提供之賠償外，尚需承擔與工作相關之聲請。
與本公司負債相關之風險
本公司可能無法產生足夠之現金流量以償付債務本息及其他義務。

我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果可能受多種因素影響，無論是否為現有或未知，包括但不限於以下所描述的內容。任何這些因素都可能，直接或間接，使我們的實際財務狀況與營運結果與向前看陳述中預期、預測或假設的結果有重大差異。任何這些因素，全部或部分，都可能對我們的業務、前景、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流與股票價格產生重大且不利的影響。這些也可能受到適用於所有公司的一般因素影響，而這些因素並未在以下特別說明。本節的揭露反映我們對可能對我們未來產生重大且不利影響的因素的信念與意見。對過往事件的參考僅為範例，並非完整清單，也並非表示這些因素是否曾發生過或其未來發生的可能性。
以下為一些可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與未來前景產生重大且不利影響的主要風險與不確定性之摘要。您應與以下更詳細說明每個風險因素的描述一併閱讀。
與我們的業務與產業相關的風險
我們服務的需求在很大程度上取決於客戶的資本支出水平。石油與天然氣產業的衰退往往導致客戶支出減少，並降低對我們服務的需求，這在過去已對我們的財務狀況、營運結果與現金流產生重大不利影響，未來也可能產生相同影響。
石油與天然氣資源生產量的增加可能導致供給增加，而需求卻沒有相應成長，這可能會對石油與天然氣價格產生負面影響。
